CHALLENGE. PUSH: the creature stands, then a horizontal shove of 0.15 s is applied to the torso. For each seed the largest survivable shove is searched forwards and backwards (up to a ceiling). Score = the smaller of the two critical forces in newtons (higher is better); PASS needs score >= challenge.target_force.

HOW YOU ARE JUDGED. Your proposals are untrusted. ACCEPTANCE RULE (verdict_v1): on held-out seeds, paired with the unchanged creature, the median per-seed gain in critical push force must be at least 3 N and at least 10% of the original's median; forces are measured to 0.625 N, and the gains must be consistent across seeds (one-sided sign test, p < 0.05). A change smaller than this is recorded as not verified even if it helps a little, so size each edit to the effect you predict (within the edit rules below).

EVIDENCE. The user message lists every measurement as one `path=value` line; these paths are the ONLY citable ones. Seeds are ordered worst to best by score (seeds[0] is the worst). Derived: leg_length = thigh + shank; foot_to_leg = mean foot length / mean leg length; weight_n = mass_total * 9.81; torque_to_weight = torque_limit / (weight_n * mean leg length); heel_behind_ankle_* and toe_ahead_of_ankle_* = how far each sole reaches behind / in front of its ankle in the compiled model (both scale with foot_length). - torso_mass [morphology; targets both] torso mass parameter (kg); sets the torso box density
- thigh_length [morphology; targets both|rear|front] thigh length, hip to knee (m)
- shank_length [morphology; targets both|rear|front] shank length, knee to ankle (m)
- foot_length [morphology; targets both|rear|front] foot length (m); the foot extends mostly forward of the ankle
- leg_density [morphology; targets both] density of every leg segment incl. feet (kg/m^3)
- foot_friction [morphology; targets both] foot-floor Coulomb friction coefficient
- torque_limit [actuation; targets both] motor torque limit of every joint (N*m)
- stand.kp [control; targets both] joint position-gain (N*m/rad) of the standing PD controller
- stand.kd [control; targets both] joint damping gain (N*m*s/rad) of the standing PD controller

diagnosis.summary: The backward weakness stems from inadequate ankle torque generation relative to the disturbance impulse, causing loss of angular momentum control rather than foot slip. Evidence shows ankle torque demand hits limits early in the backward direction while foot slip plays a minor role.

hypotheses.mechanism: Ankle torque saturation occurs earlier in backward push due to poorer leverage from foot geometry, causing angular momentum buildup and backward fall before slip can develop.
competing: Foot slip is the primary cause of failure.

hypotheses.mechanism: Insufficient forward foot extension reduces the ability to generate a forward ground reaction force during backward push, limiting ankle torque production and causing premature instability.
competing: Increasing foot length would not improve torque generation due to actuator limits.

proposals.tradeoffs: May reduce forward clearance slightly; minimal impact on forward push.
proposals.verification: Based on prior similar edits showing improved backward stability via increased lever arm for ankle torque.

selection.rule: Screening only selects. Best AI arm = highest MEDIAN screening score among AI arms (ties: higher mean, then arm order); best baseline = the same rule among random_baseline + heuristic arms. Arms with any ERROR seed are excluded and listed. Validation (held-out seeds, original + selected arms + the selected AI arm's own matched-random twin, so every AI verdict has a like-for-like control on the same seeds) decides via verdict_v1. Model confidence is never read.
